title: Quick quiz: how solar panels work
intro: Ten questions on the technology. Tap an answer to see why.
messages: Worth another read of the guide above.

qs.q: What do solar panels turn into electricity?
qs.why: Panels use the photovoltaic effect: light knocks electrons loose in the cells, which creates current.

qs.q: Do solar panels still make power on a cloudy day?
options: Yes, and just as much as on a sunny day
qs.why: Clouds scatter light but do not block all of it. Output drops, often by half or more, but it does not go to zero.

options: Energy made or used over time
qs.why: A 5 kW system running at full output for one hour makes 5 kWh. Your power bill is billed in kWh.

qs.q: In the northern hemisphere, which roof face usually gets the most sun?
qs.why: South-facing roofs see the sun all day. East and west faces still work well, with somewhat less yearly output.

qs.q: How does cold weather affect solar panels?
options: Panels often work a little better when cool
They need a heater to start
qs.why: Panels lose a little output when hot. Cold, bright days can be very productive.

options: Changes the panels' DC power into AC power for your home
qs.why: Panels make direct current. Your home and the grid use alternating current.

qs.q: Part of your roof is shaded in the afternoon. What can limit the loss?
qs.why: These devices let each panel work on its own, so one shaded panel does not drag the others down.

qs.q: Your roof has about three years of life left. What is the smart move?
options: Replace the roof before installing panels
Install panels first and replace the roof later
Panels will protect the old roof, so do nothing
qs.why: Panels last 25 years or more. Taking them off to re-roof later costs money, so fix an ageing roof first.

qs.q: How long is a common performance warranty on solar panels?
qs.why: Most makers promise a set output (often 80 to 90 percent) after 25 years.

qs.q: A grid-tied solar system has no battery. The grid goes down. What happens?
options: The system shuts off for safety
It keeps the whole house running
qs.why: Without a battery and backup wiring, panels must stop so they do not send power into lines that crews are working on.
